title: Why you forget what you came in for

lines.text: Ever walk into a room and instantly forget why you went in?
It's not your memory failing. It might be the door.
Psychologist Gabriel Radvansky at the University of Notre Dame tested this.
People carried objects from room to room in a virtual building, and their memory was tested along the way.
Walking through a doorway made them forget more than walking the same distance inside one room.
Your brain seems to treat a doorway as an event boundary, like the end of a chapter.
It files the last scene away, to make room for the new one.
And going back into the first room didn't bring the memory back.
So next time you forget why you walked in, don't blame yourself. Blame the door.

sources.claim: Gabriel Radvansky (Notre Dame) found walking through doorways causes more forgetting than the same distance in one room; returning to the original room didn't help (Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 2011)
